# Test corpus (generated by native gnubg 1.08.003)

Regenerate from the repo root (about 7 seconds, deterministic; seed 12345):
`HOME=$(mktemp -d) engine/native/build/strict/gnubg -t -r -q -P engine/data -p tests/corpus/make_corpus.py`

- Every position comes from gnubg self-play (both sides 0-ply, cube in use). Nothing is typed in by hand. Each `positionId:matchId` pair is loaded back into gnubg (`gnubg.setgnubgid`) and must read back unchanged.
- `positions.json`: 43 positions. 30 `move` (dice in the match ID) and 13 `cube` (before rolling, cube available to the player on roll).
  - Move: opening 2, contact 8, DMP contact 1, crashed 2, prime 2, race 4, bearoff-ts 3 (CLASS_BEAROFF2), bearoff-os 3 (CLASS_BEAROFF1), doubles 2, no-move 1, forced (one legal move) 1, bar 1.
  - Cube, by gnubg's 2-ply verdict: no double 2, double/take 2, double/pass 2, too good/take 1, too good/pass 1, beaver 2, optional double (post-Crawford) 1, redouble with cube 2 or 4 owned by the roller 2.
  - Scores: money 19 (Jacoby on 9, off 10) and match 24 (5-pt 9, 7-pt 8, Crawford 2, post-Crawford 3, DMP 2). Cube values 1, 2 and 4 occur, owned by either side.
- `nativeHintAtCreation`: for moves, gnubg's default 2-ply hint (top 3 moves). For cubes, `cfevaluate` at 2-ply with beavers allowed in money play. These values are for reference only. The real comparison should be recomputed in a fresh process (see NOTES.md, the 1-ulp history issue).
- `matches/`: self-play with fixed seeds, saved with `save match` (.sgf) and `export match mat` (.mat), with the bots' move lists cleared.
  - `match5`: 5-point match, 4 games.
  - `match7`: 7-point match, 3 games.
  - `money4`: money session, Jacoby off, 4 games.
  - All three include at least one double/pass and at least one resignation.
  - Each .sgf re-imports to the same moves as its .mat.
  - The files carry the run date, so they differ from day to day. `positions.json` does not.
- Things to know:
  - Beavers are not in the match ID. They are a global gnubg setting (`set beavers`, default 3).
  - Jacoby is bit 66 of the match ID, stored inverted. Match-play IDs here have it off.
  - Money match IDs carry the running session score, which has no effect on play.
  - `nativeClass` depends on which bearoff databases are loaded (here `gnubg_ts0.bd` and `gnubg_os0.bd`).
